description: Research Experiences for Undergraduates (REU), NSF NHERI 2025: Depth Monitoring of Crack-Induced Erosion in Centrifuge Testing is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "other", published or maintained by Troy Olson, University of California Davis (ucdavis.edu). This project focuses on monitoring crack-induced erosion in levees using centrifuge modeling and a low-cost RGB–D camera. The system captures continuous 3D data on crack widening, erosion depth, and volume loss, offering insights that traditional methods miss. The data can be reused to validate numerical models, compare monitoring techniques, and advance geotechnical research. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "other" project with 3 top-level files (PPTX, DOCX). Its DOI is 10.17603/ds2-5qem-gr84. Keywords: Center for Geotechnical Modeling at UC Davis,  centrifuge modeling, crack widening, rgb-d,  Realsense D435, erosion. Published 2025-08-26. Facility named: Center for Geotechnical Modeling - University of California, Davis. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is CC-BY-4.0 (labelled "Creative Commons Attribution" on the DesignSafe project). Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
